notes:
**Windows** — run `ruze_0.0.60_x64-setup.exe`.
**macOS** — open `ruze_0.0.60_universal.dmg` and drag Ruze into Applications. macOS 12 or newer, Apple Silicon or Intel. Ruze is not notarized by Apple, so the first time macOS will refuse to open it: go to System Settings → Privacy & Security, and choose *Open Anyway* beside the message about Ruze.
**Linux** — `flatpak install ruze-0.0.60.flatpak`, then `flatpak run com.ruze.chat`.
**Android** — sideload `ruze-0.0.60.apk`. arm64 devices, Android 8.0 or newer.
**iOS** — sideload `ruze-0.0.60.ipa` with AltStore, SideStore or Sideloadly, which sign it with your own Apple ID. iOS 15 or newer. Ruze is not on the App Store; with a free Apple ID the install has to be refreshed every seven days, which those tools do for you.
**VPS** — `ruzed-0.0.60-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` (or `-aarch64`) is the daemon a server can be hosted on, for a Linux machine you run. The README inside says how to set it up. On a Windows machine, run `ruzed-0.0.60-windows-x86_64-setup.exe`, which installs it as a service.

---

Ruze runs on a Mac, and on an iPhone.

### Added

- **There is a macOS version.** One download, `ruze_0.0.60_universal.dmg`,
  runs natively on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs with macOS 12 or newer. It
  lives in the menu bar the way it lives in the tray elsewhere: closing the
  window keeps you online, the menu bar icon and the Dock icon bring it back,
  and ⌘Q quits. Voice asks for the microphone the first time you join a call.
  Ruze is not notarized by Apple, so the first time you open it macOS will
  refuse. Go to System Settings → Privacy & Security and choose *Open Anyway*.
  After that it opens normally. When there is a new version, the app tells
  you and opens the download. Push to talk on a mouse button is not available
  on the Mac yet; keyboard shortcuts work.
- **There is an iOS version.** `ruze-0.0.60.ipa` is the same app as on
  Android — your account, your friends and your servers, with the camera to
  scan the code that links it to a device you are already signed in on. It
  needs iOS 15 or newer. It is not on the App Store yet, so it is installed by
  sideloading: AltStore, SideStore or Sideloadly sign it with your own Apple
  ID. With a free Apple ID the install has to be refreshed every seven days,
  which those tools do for you. The iOS app does not check for updates
  itself; new versions will come from the App Store.

### Fixed

- **On a phone, the app stays the size of the screen.** Tapping into the
  message box on an iPhone zoomed the whole app in and left it that way, with
  the server list half off the left of the screen and your name and settings
  off the right. A pinch did the same on Android. The app no longer zooms.
- **On an iPhone, nothing sits under the clock.** The top of every screen was
  drawn beneath the status bar and the Dynamic Island, and turning the phone
  on its side put the notch over the server list. Both are clear now.
